liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Me & My Uncle** (1 review): Highlights one of the first times the band played this song, noting high energy [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-12-01.149985.sbd.pnp.lestakatt.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 177 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd66-12-01.sbd.ladner.8575.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 134 min; rated 3.94/5 by 18 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer notes the classic mid-60s Dead sound, though quality is merely acceptable for the era; Sound quality is poor, but the performance sounds more like the Animals than the Dead [6][12]
- **gd66-12-01.sbd.sirmick.26968.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 133 min; rated 3.73/5 by 30 [5]. Said about its sound: This cleaned-up version is considerably less noisy than the previous copy of the show; The Cream Puff War track is corrupted, forcing the listener to use an MP3 instead [13][16]
- **gd1966-12-01.sbd.32800.shnf**: soundboard; 27 songs; 148 min; rated 3.22/5 by 9 [2]

## Around the show

- Believes Paul Butterfield plays harmonica on this track, as he does on his first album [10]
- Explains Deep Elem was a Dallas area with live music venues and brothels in the 1920s-30s [11]
- The Grateful Dead were booked for four nights, November 28 through December 1, 1966 [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-12-01.149985.sbd.pnp.lestakatt.flac1644**: transferred by Pitch Correction and minor editing/crossfading. Fixed by Michael Lestatkatt.; source: SBD>MR>RR>C>DAT [1]. Also: Pitch corrected in 2014 but never shared; original source details cannot be confirmed by the uploader [1]
- **gd66-12-01.sbd.ladner.8575.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by C.M.; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: A lower-generation Viola Lee recording from this show masquerades as the first song from March 12, 1966; Signal path: SBD to RM to Reel to Dat to CD to wav to shnv3 [3][15]
- **gd66-12-01.sbd.sirmick.26968.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1966-12-01.sbd.32800.shnf**: source: SBD>MR>RR>C>DAT [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Crimson Records: [GRATEFUL DEAD - Two Days At The Matrix 1966 - Crimson Records](https://crimsonrecords.com.ar/product/grateful-dead-two-days-at-the-matrix-1966/) [22]
